item: fts_status takes rows from the articles' covering-index count instead of a scan of the full-text table: 35 times cheaper cold at 1,000,000 articles; the premise that a count of articles is a corpus scan is withdrawn
summary: Follow-on to #1534, from the WAL lane's cold encrypted measurement at 1,000,000 articles (R295). Step 3 of fts_status read SELECT count(*) FROM article_fts; for an external-content FTS5 table that reads every row of the content table, so it cost a table scan of articles (9.6 to 11.9 s cold, 5.5 to 6.0 s warm, 99% of the call, 3 to 5 s from its own 15 s deadline, and it follows the article TEXT, so a real store would time out at far fewer articles) to give the number that count(*) FROM articles gives from the covering index idx_article_created_at in 0.25 s cold. NOW: rows is SELECT count(*) FROM articles inside the same count deadline; count_status, the probe, #1534's one-statement ends and population, and every key and label are unchanged. fts_status whole, cold, 5 runs on the same encrypted store: 292 / 327 / 558 ms (min / median / max) against 9,729 / 11,382 / 11,975; warm 2.1 / 2.3 / 2.8 against 5,539 / 5,801 / 6,009; corpus_integrity cold 11.7 / 12.6 / 15.0 s against 17.2 / 17.3 / 17.4 (the rest is PRAGMA foreign_key_check, 11 to 14 s, untouched). The docstrings of ensure_fts and fts_status no longer say a count of articles is a corpus scan (the 74 s cold figure on a 2.7 GB corpus was not reproduced on the current schema); the boot still compares no counts, left as a decision. Tests: the five that simulated the old statement are rewritten, the prefix test that pinned 'no statement counts the articles' now pins one plain count with a covering-index plan and nothing counting article_fts, rows equals the old statement over a full / shrunken / emptied / partial index, a partial index still reads partial (inferred) with the count answered and timed out, and the count runs inside a deadline; 8 of 8 mutants red. LIMITS: one machine and a fast virtual disk, synthetic Latin text of 1.3 KB per article, nothing above 1 M; the plan is the planner's choice (pinned on the real schema); the integrity report's own second count of articles and its foreign_key_check (90% of the report cold, on a store with no keyword rows) are unchanged.
